measurement: the churn arm: does a transcript survive its neighbour count moving underneath it
question: The constant levels pin occupancy at N with a semaphore that refills the instant a clip finishes, so a session never sees its neighbour count move far. This admits on a triangle wave 1 -> N -> 1 every 20 s, so a 33 s utterance lives through a full cycle.
prediction_made_before_the_run: Ragged under churn should diverge MORE than ragged at constant occupancy, because the batch shape now moves within a session's life as well as between runs. If it did not, the model of the mechanism would be wrong.
reads: Fixed padding under churn is INVARIANT: one digest across 1 / 32a / 32b / churned 42. A session living through its neighbour count swinging 1 -> 42 -> 1 repeatedly produces the same transcript as the same audio run alone. This was the last untested arm of the claim.

The prediction holds on the comparison that tests it. Ragged max-vs-1 goes from 66 streams differing at constant occupancy to 88 when churned -- a third more. The shape moving within a session does break more transcripts than the shape merely being larger.

Read the right comparison. The gate's headline counts the UNION over all pairs, which is dominated by the 32-vs-1 comparisons (118 streams in both runs), so the union moves the other way (128 -> 120) while the arm under test moves up. The union is not the measurement.

The gate is reproducible. Across two independent ragged runs, levels 1, 32a and 32b give byte-identical digests and identical divergence counts; only the churned level differs, which is the only thing that was changed.
The churned level took 92.5 s against 57.9 s constant, and on the fixed arm 87.5 s against 57.9 s: the wave really does hold occupancy down for part of every cycle.
unfinished: ChurnGate records the in-flight count at each admission (observed_occupancy) so a run can show its wave rather than assert it, and that is not yet plumbed into the record. With it, a diverging stream could be correlated with whether it was admitted at the trough or the crest, which is the obvious next question and cannot be answered from this run.
